question.problem:
Find the sum modulo $33$ of the solutions to the congruence $15x≡18\,(\text{mod}\,33).$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*
question.worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=15$ and $n=33$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(15,33)=3.
$$

Since $b=18$ is divisible by $3,$ our congruence has $3$ solutions.

First, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}15x & ≡18 &  & (\text{mod}\,33) \\ 3\cdot 5x & ≡3\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,3\cdot 11) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot 5x & ≡\cancel{3}\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{3}\cdot 11) \\ 5x & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the new congruence above, we have ${a}_{1}=5$ and ${n}_{1}=11$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(5,11)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $11.$
To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,11).$ And to find the inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,11),$ we compute the exponents of $5\,(\text{mod}\,11)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,11):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡25≡2\cdot 11+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {5}^{3} & ≡3\cdot 5≡15≡11+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {5}^{4} & ≡4\cdot 5≡20≡11+9≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {5}^{5} & ≡9\cdot 5≡45≡4\cdot 11+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $9\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,11),$ which means that $9$ is the multiplicative inverse of $5$ (modulo $11$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $9,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ 9\cdot 5x & ≡9\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ (9\cdot 5)x & ≡54 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ x & ≡54 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ x & ≡4\cdot 11+10 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ x & ≡10 &  & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡10\,(\text{mod}\,11).$ 

But our original congruence was modulo $33$ (not modulo $11$). To find all the solutions modulo $33,$ we repeatedly add $11$ modulo $33$ until we reach the number $10$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡10 &  & (\text{mod}\,33) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡10+11≡21 &  & (\text{mod}\,33) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡21+11≡32 &  & (\text{mod}\,33) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡32+11≡43≡1\cdot 33+10≡10≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,18)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x≡10,21,32\,(\text{mod}\,33).$ 

Finally,

$$
10+21+32≡63≡33+30≡30\,(\text{mod}\,33).
$$
